Stochastic spreading of phase coordinates over time.
An ordered deformation that changes relative phase relations across a trajectory while preserving selected endpoint constraints.
A reordering of phase-mode labels used as a control or transformation; semantics must declare whether labels are exchangeable.
A reduction of a higher-dimensional state to a two-dimensional spinor/Bloch description for a declared task.
Loss of locally identifiable directions caused by a lower-rank projection; for the declared 36D to SU2 summary rank is at most 2 versus 35 in the baseline QFIM.
The property that a reduced representation retains all information needed for a declared task, without claiming global faithfulness.
The magnitude of the circular mean phasor used to quantify phase concentration across components.
The argument of the mean unit phasor for angular data.
A bounded interval over which relations are jointly considered when defining a temporally extended state.
Dependence of a present organization on a nonzero interval of past and/or anticipated future states.
Persistence of information from immediately preceding states into current processing.
Representation or constraint of possible future states that influences present processing.
Coordination of events or representations across time into a structured sequence or episode.
The extent of past and future relations available to current processing or control.
The furthest time scale over which a system explicitly represents relevant possible states or consequences.
Duration over which a state, relation, goal, or pattern remains effective under declared conditions.
Combination of information across time such that earlier and later states mutually constrain interpretation or action.
A disruption in the relations that normally link successive states into a continuous trajectory.
The ordering relation among events or states used by a model of history or sequence.
Memory for ordered relations among events or items rather than only their occurrence.
Temporary maintenance and manipulation of information for current cognition and action.
Memory for personally situated events including contextual and temporal relations.
Memory for concepts, facts, and relations abstracted from specific episodes.
Memory contributing to a person or agent model of its own history across episodes.
Memory for intended future actions or conditions to be recognized later.
Memory expressed in acquired skills or procedures rather than primarily explicit declarative recall.
Memory for the origin or context in which information was acquired.
A graded sense or signal that current content has been encountered before, separable from detailed recollection.
Retrieval involving structured contextual details of a prior event or state.
Processes by which current information changes a memory-bearing substrate or state.
Persistence of encoded information in a form capable of later influence or retrieval.
Processes that make stored information available to current processing.
A current state or signal that changes the probability or form of memory retrieval.
The ease or probability with which stored information can be brought into current use.
Agreement of a retrieved or reconstructed memory with a declared reference about the past.
A confidence estimate associated with a memory judgment; it is not identical to memory accuracy.
Reported or measured richness/intensity of a recalled experience; it is not identical to accuracy.
Modification of a memory after reactivation before it returns to a more persistent state.
Reduced accessibility or influence of previously encoded information over time.
Impairment of new learning or retrieval caused by earlier learned information.
Impairment of older information caused by later learning or activity.
Continuity of self-related memory relations across time contributing to identity organization.
The relation by which selected memories become integrated into a maintained model of the same persisting self.
The total structured content present for a subject at a time or over a declared temporal window.
What is experienced within a phenomenal field, distinguished from the access/report mechanisms that may describe it.
The way an experience feels or is presented for the subject, as distinct from its external stimulus label.
